clue.text: Frost? Sounds like it could be a piece of poetry

indicators.note: says we want a word pronounced the same as the poetic term that follows

blocks.note: a rhyme is a short piece of verse

explanation.surface: Someone muses that the word frost has the ring of a poem about it.
explanation.walkthrough: RIME and RHYME are pronounced identically.
explanation.definitionFit: Rime is the white feathery ice deposit that forms on cold surfaces, a type of frost.

clue.text: Revolutionary annoyed humanitarian organisation

blocks.note: red is a common label for a revolutionary or communist
cross means annoyed

explanation.surface: An angry rebel turns on an aid agency.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Cross is the international movement giving medical and disaster relief, a charitable body.

clue.text: Prophet some stoned, leader of sect

indicators.note: stoned means intoxicated, so the letters are in a confused state and need sorting
the leader of a word is its opening letter, so take just that

blocks.note: taken as written
first letter of sect

explanation.surface: A prophet, the head of a sect, has had some followers stoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stoned' summons the biblical punishment, but here it means high.
explanation.definitionFit: Moses is the Old Testament prophet who led the Israelites out of Egypt.

clue.text: Pity padre breaking original of rock'n'roll Beatles' record

indicators.note: something breaking falls apart, so these letters come apart and are rearranged
the original of a word is where it begins, so take only its opening letter

blocks.note: taken as written
first letter of rock'n'roll

explanation.surface: A rocker complains that a sorry clergyman smashed up a classic Beatles disc.
explanation.definitionFit: Day Tripper was a 1965 Beatles single, released as a double A-side with We Can Work It Out.

clue.text: A monk embracing a bishop in a state

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug, so the monk's letters enclose what follows

blocks.note: taken as written
a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist monk
taken as written
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A monk hugs a bishop, and both are in a right state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a state' sounds like agitation; 'a state' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabama is one of the United States, in the Deep South.

clue.text: Go round in still ascending tramcar

indicators.note: in a down clue, ascending means reading upwards, so the word runs backwards
one item placed inside another, so the circling word goes within

blocks.note: yet means still, as in 'not yet'
to roll is to turn round and round

explanation.surface: A tram still climbs uphill as it goes round the loop.
explanation.definitionFit: A trolley, or trolley car, is a tram powered from an overhead wire, chiefly in American usage.

clue.text: Weapon that's caused row to flare up?

definitions.text: Weapon that's caused row to flare up?

blocks.clueFragment: Weapon that's caused row to flare up?
blocks.note: surface reading: an inflammatory remark that sparked a quarrel
setter's reading: a device that sets a row of buildings ablaze

explanation.surface: Someone asks what verbal ammunition turned a dispute into a blazing argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests an argument and 'flare up' a temper, but literally the weapon sets a row of houses on fire.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an explosive designed to start fires, dropped from aircraft in wartime raids.

clue.text: Stupidly obstinate, as Napoleon was shown to be?

definitions.text: as Napoleon was shown to be?

blocks.note: first meaning: stubborn beyond reason

blocks.clueFragment: as Napoleon was shown to be?
blocks.note: second meaning: in Orwell's Animal Farm the tyrant Napoleon is a pig, so leads as a pig at the head

explanation.walkthrough: The obvious Napoleon is the French emperor; the one meant is the boar who rules Orwell's Animal Farm.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes mulish stubbornness, and literally fits a pig who is the farm's leader.

clue.text: River (Italian) full of fish? Just the opposite — an unusual thing

indicators.note: 'Just the opposite' flips this: rather than the river holding the fish, the fish is filled with the river

blocks.note: a ray is a flat fish
R is the abbreviation for river
It is the abbreviation for Italian

explanation.surface: An Italian river teems with fish, or rather the reverse, which would be odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just the opposite' reverses which part holds which: the fish goes outside the river and the Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: A rarity is something seldom found, an uncommon object or occurrence.

clue.text: Drink, sweetish — new lot ordered

indicators.note: ordered means put into a fresh sequence, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A drinker orders a fresh round of something on the sweet side.
explanation.definitionFit: To wet one's whistle is an idiom for having a drink, especially to quench thirst.

clue.text: Outlaw dead? Rope's frayed

indicators.note: a frayed rope has its strands come loose and jumbled, so these letters are disordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An outlaw's hanging failed because the rope had worn through.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless bandit of the Wild West kind, a criminal living outside the law.

clue.text: US soldier getting back in vehicle for a smoke

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the letters are read right to left
one item sits inside another, so the soldier's letters go within the vehicle's

blocks.note: GI is the standard term for an American private soldier
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: An American serviceman climbs back into his car to have a smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: A cigar is a roll of tobacco leaf that one smokes, so it can stand for a smoke.

clue.text: Rash girl, the Parisienne after ring

indicators.note: after means coming behind, so the French word is placed following the round letter rather than before it

blocks.note: Rose is a girl's name
a ring is round like the letter O
la is the French feminine word for the

explanation.surface: A girl rashly gets engaged, like some impetuous young woman from Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rash' looks like an adjective about the girl, but it is the noun definition. 'After ring' places the French article behind O.
explanation.definitionFit: Roseola is a rosy skin rash, typically from a childhood viral infection.

clue.text: Let about nine off, being merciful

indicators.note: something off is not right or out of order, so the number's letters are scrambled
about means surrounding, so the first word's letters wrap round the others

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A kindly judge lets around nine offenders off.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenient means mild and tolerant in punishing, which is to show mercy.

clue.text: Flyer given out by PA in front of prison?

blocks.note: a PA, a personal assistant, is a secretary
bird is British slang for a prison sentence (from rhyming slang bird-lime, time)

explanation.surface: A personal assistant hands out leaflets outside a jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flyer' suggests a handbill being distributed; it is in fact a bird. 'In front of' puts the PA before the prison.
explanation.definitionFit: The secretary bird is a long-legged African bird of prey, so a creature that flies.

clue.text: Bobby studies list

blocks.note: to con is to study or learn by heart, an old sense
a table is a list of data

explanation.surface: Bobby is poring over a list.
explanation.walkthrough: A bobby is British slang for a police officer, after Sir Robert Peel; 'Bobby' looks like a person's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A constable is a police officer of the lowest rank, which is what a bobby is.

clue.text: Protest about despicable person, a party member

blocks.note: a demo is a protest march
c is short for circa, about
a rat is a despicable person

explanation.surface: Demonstrators decry some contemptible figure in a political party.
explanation.definitionFit: A Democrat belongs to the US Democratic Party, one of the two main American parties.

clue.text: Toy owls entranced cuckoo

indicators.note: cuckoo means crazy, so the preceding words are mixed up madly

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird-themed toy has hypnotised owls, and a cuckoo too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuckoo' fits the birds of the surface but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Newton's cradle is the executive desk toy of swinging steel balls demonstrating momentum.

clue.text: Ham — pile it on

blocks.note: first meaning: to perform in an exaggerated theatrical way
second meaning: to exaggerate or overdo things

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ham' tempts as the meat stacked on a plate; here it is a verb about bad acting.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are verbs for exaggerating, whether on stage or in everyday behaviour.

clue.text: Odd sea term for a vessel

indicators.note: odd means strange or irregular, so the letters are in an unusual order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on a curious nautical word for a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamer is a steamship, a vessel driven by steam engines.

clue.text: An angelic being — apprentice is full of her

indicators.note: being full of something means holding it inside, so the pronoun goes within

blocks.note: a cub is a novice or trainee, as in cub reporter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A trainee is utterly smitten with her, thinking her angelic.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherub is a winged angel of the second order, often shown as a chubby child.

clue.text: Communications link arranged in hotel

indicators.note: arranged means set in a new order, so the letters are put into another sequence

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A phone connection has been set up at the hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotline is a direct telephone line for urgent contact, a dedicated channel of communication.

clue.text: Official ban therefore must include male graduate

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it within, so the other letters go inside

blocks.note: ergo is Latin for therefore
M is the abbreviation for male
a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A ruling is laid down that a man with a degree must be admitted.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is a government order prohibiting trade or activity, a formal prohibition.

clue.text: Treasure-trove, in part, is reminiscent of the past

indicators.note: in part means only a portion is used, so the letters lie within the phrase

blocks.note: the letters run across the hyphen

explanation.surface: Buried treasure partly evokes bygone days.
explanation.definitionFit: Retro describes styles that imitate or recall earlier decades.

clue.text: Programmed machine in part of plant to check blood group

indicators.note: to check is to hold back or restrain, so the outer word holds the other inside it

blocks.note: the root is the underground part of a plant
B is one of the ABO blood groups

explanation.surface: A machine in a factory is set to test blood samples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' suggests a factory, which suits a machine, but here it is a growing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A robot is an automated device that carries out a sequence of actions set by its software.

clue.text: School one attended with girl friend close to Chester

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so take only its final letter

blocks.note: Alma is a girl's name
a mate is a friend
last letter of Chester

explanation.surface: Someone recalls their old school, attended with a girlfriend near Chester.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Girl friend' reads as one word, girlfriend, but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Alma mater, Latin for nourishing mother, is the school or university a person once went to.

clue.text: Bodyguards in action against European spiking drinks

indicators.note: spiking a drink means slipping something into it, so these letters go inside the drinks

blocks.note: beers are drinks
E is the abbreviation for European
a feat is a deed or action; 'against' places it beside the European

explanation.surface: Security men take action against a European suspected of spiking drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: Beefeaters are the Yeomen Warders of the Tower of London, and formally the Yeomen of the Guard, the monarch's bodyguard.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yeomen of the Guard, popularly called Beefeaters, are the sovereign's ceremonial bodyguard.

clue.text: Letters should get one a job

blocks.note: first meaning: the mail delivered to a house
second meaning: a position of employment

explanation.surface: Writing letters of application ought to land you employment.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the British term for mail and a word for a paid position held by someone.
